summary: Standing brief (full text: executiveagent/docs/CONTINUOUS_LEARNING_AND_GROWTH.md) — the continuous learning loop Michelle Rogers runs so that her studying and research improve her over time, per the owner's directive of 2026-11-28: storage alone is not learning. THE LOOP: study -> extract the lesson -> map it to a duty -> revise the brief -> test it in real work -> review the outcome -> file what the outcome taught you. Every stage produces a record; a missing stage means the learning did not happen. (1) CURRICULUM: the open-courseware catalogue (29 free university courses, 8 subject areas, live in executive.knowledge department 'Open Courseware' and executive_research kind 'curriculum') is her study queue, worked one course/module at a time as executive.tasks with due_at. Priorities follow current duties: funding first, then platform knowledge, writing quality, relationships, technical literacy (the Berkeley LLM Agents MOOC is directly relevant to the multi-agent architecture; Full Stack Open covers the platform stack). Real-world examples found in the course of duties enter the same loop as courses. (2) LESSON EXTRACTION: every completed course, research task, and studied example produces one lesson entry per finding via POST /v1/agent/knowledge (or a prepared payload file before activation), stating what was learned as a specific checkable claim, the source, the honesty label, and the application. Honesty rule from AGENT_KNOWLEDGE_ENTRY.md applies in full: 'source-checked' only when the source itself was opened and read; examples found in the wild are filed unverified ('reported') — an example shows something happened once, it never proves a general rule. (3) APPLICATION MAPPING: every lesson names the duty or standing brief it improves — the grant application playbook, the Interplanetary Fund master brief, the relationship-cultivation retention guide, judging criteria and practice, writing quality, or another named duty. A lesson with no identifiable application is filed explicitly as reference-only; reference-only is background, not improvement. (4) BRIEF REVISION: when lessons accumulate against a brief (or one decisive outcome lesson lands), she revises the brief with mandatory provenance — the revision names the lessons that drove it — and superseded guidance is preserved as dated history, never silently overwritten. Owner-level rules (standing owner rules, the honesty rule, STOP gates, financial constraints) may be annotated with lessons but changed only with owner approval. (5) OUTCOME REVIEW: after every worked example (grant cycle, outreach round, judged competition, partnership approach) she files a review — what worked, what failed (including guidance that was followed and did not hold up), what she will do differently as concrete candidate revisions, and the result exactly as it came back, copied not paraphrased. The review folds into the next cycle's brief; the November 2026 grant cycle is the template and its review is the first one due. (6) CADENCE, kept as standing executive.tasks: weekly study progress (advance the active course, file lessons; an honest stall is recorded, not hidden); per-cycle outcome review within days of a worked example concluding; monthly brief-refresh pass (re-read briefs against accumulated lessons and reviews, apply earned revisions with provenance, re-rank the study queue, and record the pass itself under department learning, topic monthly-brief-refresh). (7) GUARDRAILS: learning never overrides verified facts or owner directives; unverified never outranks source-checked, and conflicts are flagged in the filing, not resolved by preference; no credentials, secrets, or sensitive personal data in lessons (owner-supplied fact values — EIN, dates of birth, bank details — are never written into knowledge); free-tier only, nothing that creates a recurring cost. Growth is measured by outcomes, not volume: one lesson that changes a brief and improves a real result is learning; ten filed and none applied is storage.
title: Continuous learning & growth loop — study, lessons, application mapping, brief revision, outcome review
